edges.rationale: Git history was evaluated as a possible knowledge source.
Ordinary documentation was evaluated as a possible knowledge source.
Commit ancestry does not encode accepted semantic state.
Hand-maintained prose cannot prove freshness or authority.
The accepted protocol required an executable trust root and CLI.
The implementation made accepted knowledge the product boundary.
A single-document authority model was considered.
Separate authority layers were the alternative.
Documents cannot distinguish recomputable facts from accepted meaning.
The approved model begins with recomputable facts.
Facts and reviewed meaning require separate durable records.
Accepted history requires candidate changes to remain untrusted until validated.
Validated proposals need an atomic application boundary.
Accepted candidate state enables deterministic human views.
The transaction boundary is implemented with the other knowledge layers.
Projection contracts complete the implementation scope.
The completed layers support machine validation and human views.

nodes.description: Make repository intent, accepted decisions, evidence, and current meaning survive tool and maintainer changes.
nodes.title: Preserve durable repository knowledge

nodes.description: Infer current intent from commits and pull-request history instead of maintaining accepted semantic records.
nodes.title: Treat Git history as sufficient knowledge

nodes.description: Keep architecture and operating knowledge in conventional Markdown without machine validation.
nodes.title: Use ordinary hand-maintained documentation

nodes.description: Use Git as durable storage while adding explicit semantic records, evidence rules, validation, and deterministic views.
nodes.title: Create a repository-local knowledge protocol

nodes.description: Build the schemas, extractors, validators, transactions, and public CLI that enforce the accepted model.
nodes.title: Implement the LORE trust root and CLI

nodes.description: Generated prose is an output; the durable product is accepted, evidence-backed repository knowledge and its maintenance protocol.
nodes.title: LORE became more than a documentation generator

nodes.description: Avoid collapsing deterministic observations, reviewed semantics, and generated prose into one authority surface.
nodes.title: Separate facts, accepted meaning, and views

nodes.description: Treat generated or hand-maintained prose as the single repository knowledge representation.
nodes.title: Collapse all knowledge into documents

nodes.description: Give deterministic facts, reviewed records, transactions, and projections distinct schemas and authority boundaries.
nodes.title: Separate authority layers

nodes.description: Derive machine facts from source using configured extractors and make them reproducible.
nodes.title: Make extracted facts deterministic

nodes.description: Preserve revisions and supersession instead of rewriting earlier accepted claims in place.
nodes.title: Represent accepted history as append-only records

nodes.description: A proposal is not accepted history until schema, evidence, and source-state checks pass.
nodes.title: Treat proposals as untrusted input

nodes.description: Plan candidate state and write accepted records, receipts, and projections together with rollback on failure.
nodes.title: Apply semantic changes atomically

nodes.description: Render human-readable views from canonical state without granting those files canonical authority.
nodes.title: Generate human-readable projections

nodes.description: Implement the separately validated extraction, record, proposal, transaction, receipt, and projection layers.
nodes.title: Implement separated knowledge layers

nodes.description: LORE validates machine-readable semantic state while producing documents ordinary maintainers can read.
nodes.title: Machine state and human views coexist
